name: UL FGG
zag_role: Faculty of Civil and Geodetic Engineering, University of Ljubljana
description: ZAG's nearest academic partner, about three kilometres away. Co-supervises BRIDGITISE doctoral candidates and co-authors the Tomačevo influence-line work.
history: UL FGG is at Jamova cesta 2 in Ljubljana. Civil engineering teaching in Slovenia began in 1919, when the Department of Civil Engineering started courses at the Technical Faculty. The faculty passed through several reorganisations, becoming a department within the Technical Faculty in 1954 and part of the Faculty of Architecture, Civil and Geodetic Engineering in 1957, before becoming an independent member of the University of Ljubljana on 1 January 1995. It has three departments, Civil Engineering with twelve units including the chairs of structural and earthquake engineering, of mechanics and of geotechnical engineering, Geodetic Engineering with five chairs, and Environmental Civil Engineering. It also runs the Institute of Structural Engineering, Earthquake Engineering and Construction IT, the Water Management Institute, and hydraulic and structural testing laboratories.
